SMTO-EXE-0128 — SMTO couldn't do that web browser step as asked

GUID: 9add9e04-52b5-5fa9-977a-b46a6a2106bf
Slug: browser-invalid-request
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried a web browser step in a form it isn't allowed to use, such as opening an address that doesn't start with http:// or https://. The step was refused before anything happened on the website.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the web address you gave SMTO. It must start with http:// or https:// and must not contain a username or password, such as name:secret@ before the site name. SMTO only opens plain web addresses and refuses others, like file links or addresses with sign-in details, for safety.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to do the step again, describing the button, link or field by the words you see on the page. SMTO finds things on a page by their visible label, role or text, and refuses other ways of pointing at them.
  3. If SMTO keeps getting this message, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show which browser step was refused, which helps the person managing SMTO see what SMTO tried.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the browser step and tells you what it saw or did on the page.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details and the web address you used to the person who manages SMTO. Don't put passwords or other sign-in details into the web address to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Browser validation rejected the request before dispatch: an unknown operation, arguments that fail the operation's closed schema, a navigation URL that is not plain absolute HTTP(S), or an unsupported locator form.

What this means

  • Browser validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid closed-schema arguments, unsafe/non-HTTP(S) navigation URL or unsupported locator form. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser validation rejected an unknown operation, invalid closed-schema arguments, unsafe/non-HTTP(S) navigation URL or unsupported locator form.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the operation schema, semantic locator/exact reference and bounded URL/argument values.

How to fix it

  • Check the operation and arguments against SCHEMAS and validate() in src/gateway_core/browser/contract.py: url/initial_url must be absolute http(s) with no userinfo or control characters, locator.name requires locator.role, downloads with as_artifact needs download_id, and download_id and after_download_id cannot be combined. The request is rejected before dispatch, so no page action ran.
  • Use the advertised browser schema. Only HTTP(S) navigation, bounded arguments and semantic locators or exact refs are supported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the advertised browser schema. Only HTTP(S) navigation, bounded arguments and semantic locators or exact refs are supported.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended request validates before browser execution and stays within its owned session.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
